question: Following the first outbreak of African swine fever (ASF) detected in Spain, there have been preventive closures in more than 60 municipalities and extraordinary health control measures have been taken. The situation has raised concerns among livestock organisations about the need for effective coordination between national and regional administrations regarding wildlife management and the consistent application of biosafety protocols. 1.

Has the Spanish Government ensured immediate coordination with the Commission in order to implement joint security reinforcement mechanisms between the Commission, the Ministry of Agriculture and the Regional Government of Catalonia following the detection of the outbreak in Collserola?
Has the Spanish Government requested the dispatch of European veterinary assessment teams to verify the containment of the virus and provide technical advice on the deployment of additional measures?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (17.2.2026) The Competent Authority of Spain promptly informed the Commission about first the suspicion, and then the confirmation, of the first African swine fever (ASF) outbreak in Barcelona. Since then, the Commission is constantly informed and strictly monitors the evolution of the ASF situation as well as the implementation of all measures to avoid further disease spread.

Regional and Central Competent Authorities of Spain are working in a coordinated and efficient manner, putting in place adequate efforts and resources. So far, the disease is limited to the core area identified based on a risk assessment.

Given the urgency of the situation, the Competent Authority of Spain asked the Commission for support of the EU Veterinary Emergency Team (EUVET)1 experts that were dispatched on-the-spot in two missions, on 3-52 and 10-123 December 2025 to help handle the emergency and further investigate the origin of the virus causing the epidemic.
The Commission is in contact with the Competent Authority of Spain and promptly updates Member States and Third Countries on the evolution of the epidemiological situation.
